questions.q: In PostgreSQL, what actually determines your effective RPO, per this lesson?
options: How frequently WAL segments reach archive storage
How often the server is rebooted
The size of shared_buffers
The version of PostgreSQL installed
questions.explain: Since archive_command ships WAL segments continuously, worst-case data loss tracks that archiving interval, not the time since the last base backup.

questions.q: Why does a fresher pg_basebackup improve RTO even though WAL archiving alone could theoretically replay from any earlier point?
options: A fresher base backup means less WAL needs to be replayed to reach the recovery target, making recovery faster
Fresher backups are always smaller in file size
WAL cannot be replayed without a same-day base backup
pg_basebackup automatically deletes old WAL segments
questions.explain: Recovery time is base backup restore time plus WAL replay time since that backup — less WAL to replay means a faster recovery.

questions.q: Why does a complete PostgreSQL DR plan need a current pg_dumpall --globals-only output, per this lesson?
options: A from-scratch cluster rebuild needs roles and tablespaces recreated, which physical restores don't provide
Globals contain the actual table data
pg_basebackup automatically captures globals, so this is a backup, not a plan item
Globals are only needed for logical replication, not disaster recovery
questions.explain: Physical restores bring back data files, but a full cluster rebuild from scratch still needs cluster-wide objects like roles and tablespaces restored separately.

questions.q: What's the practical risk of an archive_command that silently fails, per this lesson?
options: WAL segments pile up unarchived and disk can fill before anyone notices, while RPO silently degrades
PostgreSQL automatically switches to logical backups instead
There is no risk, since WAL segments are always retained on disk indefinitely
The primary server immediately shuts down
questions.explain: A failing archive_command means PostgreSQL won't recycle those WAL segments, so they accumulate on disk while your actual recoverable point stops advancing.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what's true about the DBA discipline for disaster recovery across platforms?
options: The discipline (untested backups aren't real backups, RPO/RTO drive decisions) transfers directly — only the specific commands are platform-specific
Each platform requires an entirely different DR philosophy
PostgreSQL doesn't need DR planning because WAL archiving is automatic
RPO and RTO only apply to SQL Server, not open-source databases
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties this back to the same discipline applied on SQL Server, Oracle, and MySQL earlier in the path — only the mechanism changes.
